title: Learn How To Animate In Clo! Skill-Up Webinar
description:
Follow along with the files here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12gi2MP1dK5RvhKh8LGMeQaWgLHZVm9hr

This Skill-up Webinar focuses on animation features in CLO and covers motion files, converting mixamo and fbx animation files to use in CLO, the wind controller feature, camera animation, and how to render an animation. This live session took place on Nov 20, 2024. Join our next webinar to participate and ask questions live!

Chapters:
00:00 Intro
00:52 Motion Files in CLO
02:41 Animation General Overview
06:19 Mixamo Animations
10:29 New FBX Animation Conversion Feature
11:24 Opening Wind Animation File + CPU/GPU Simulation
14:50 Animation Detailed Overview, Garment Recording, FBX Export
29:36 Wind Controller Feature
40:54 Camera Animation
51:29 Render an Animation
54:34 Q&A + Outro

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord- 

--- 
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/itsclo3d 
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/clo-virtual-fashion-inc-/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/clo3d/

summary: ```markdown # Learn How To Animate In Clo! Skill-Up Webinar ## Introduction to Animation in Clo The first thing I want to tell you is about animation—where do we get animations from? Specifically, motion files. So far, you know that our avatars are quite steady. We can change the poses, but if you actually want the avatar to move, we have to do it a little bit differently. ## Locating Motion Files This is dependent on whether it's female, kids, or male avatars, located in the respective folders. In this case, we have to go to the female folder. Inside, there's a folder called 'motion.' If we open this folder, we have a selection of our default motion files that you can use on your avatar. In case you don't have everything that I have here, I just have the default version of Clo, without any specific extras downloaded. If you're not seeing this or not seeing all the avatars, it might be that behind you have small white icons with an 'N.' This means there's something new. If you have this, you can also press the download button and download these assets. But I think they should all be there. ## Using the No Hand Pose Motion File I will just continue. So, for the no hand pose, if I double-click on this, I'm prompted with a box that says, "Do you want to move the avatar and garment to the start position?" Yes. "Do you want to have a transitioning file?" Yes or no. I will explain to you what that is in a second and how long the transitioning file should be. In this case, the standard is 30 frames, and I can say okay. If I zoom out, my avatar has switched to the start position of this motion file. Then, if I want to continue to work with this, I would need to fit the garments I have onto my avatar in this position. ## Animation Tab and Timeline Next, I can go over to the drop-down menu from simulation to animation—so the animation tab. If I go to animation and zoom in a little more, you should be prompted with a different window. It has almost the same features. I can open and close my library, and I have simulation buttons here, but it's all a little bit reduced. What is new is the whole animation window that you see here. As I scroll through, you can see that the avatar then goes through the whole motion file, walks to the front, poses a little bit, and then walks back to the right side. ## Different Types of Motion Files The other motion files are almost the same. For example, one also walks to the front but does a little turn, which is made for when you have a dress. The last two motion files we have here—'walk in place' and 'idle'—are a little bit more special. 'Walk in place' allows the avatar to walk in place, and the 'idle' motion shows subtle movement, which is just for when you want to render video with almost imperceptible motion. ## Custom Animations from Mixamo If you want to do something else, where can you get custom animations? We have the option to go to a site called Mixamo. You probably heard about it before. It’s a free site from Adobe, where you just need to have an Adobe account. It has thousands of different small animations, and you can search for something like 'walk' to find different types of walks. This is mainly more for the gaming industry; it’s not super high quality, but at least you can use this and it's free. If you select something you like, you can just download it as an FBX file, which is important because this file includes the rig inside. ## Applying FBX Files to Clo Avatars Once we’ve downloaded the FBX, we can go to avatar, then 'register', and select 'convert to motion.' We will need to specify which character we want to use. This is dependent on how the hips are moving or how wide the shoulders are, for example. You can download this specifically from the Mixamo site. Now, in the 2024.2 release, you can bring in other FBX files that have not been created in Mixamo. Previously, you only had the option to use files from Mixamo. Otherwise, workflows were also possible but very difficult and only for super advanced users. ## Creating Wind Animation Let's go into our SkillUp folder here, and start with our first file called 'wind animation start.' Before we start, in the 2024.2 release, there's something added that is very useful, especially for Windows users. Now in the simulation, if you long-press, you have the possibility to switch to GPU simulation. The GPU simulation has been improved, making it more accurate in terms of collision detection and the behavior of fabrics. This speeds up your simulation by about 10-15 times. For Mac users, you are usually bound to CPU simulation due to the internal graphics. ## Setting Up the Animation Now we want to animate a beautiful dress designed by Victor. We want to load the motion file called 'walk in place.' We can create a transitioning file again, yes, and we can make it 30 frames. The motion file is loaded. At this point, the avatar is moving, but the garment is not. We need to fix that. Here on the side, this is the first thing we want to take care of—the garment animation record button. We need to play through this animation with the avatar walking, and then we’ll be ready to see how the garment behaves. ## Recording the Garment Animation We will start the simulation and just click the blue arrow to begin. We will wait a little bit; first, it will go through the transitioning file and then go through the actual walk cycle. Now that we have recorded this, you can see a new line called 'garment' that contains everything our garment is doing. If you want to get rid of parts you’re not satisfied with, you can right-click and delete them. You can also save this animation once you’re happy with it. ## Camera Animation Now I want to show you how to work with camera animation. We have a super long motion file prepared. With the new features, you can now add or exchange a keyframe for the camera, show the camera path, and add camera keyframes to create transitions. You can define where the camera will focus and how it will move through the scene. You can also adjust the field of view for a more dynamic presentation. ## Rendering the Animation To render out the animation, go to image and video properties and change this from 'single image' to 'animation.' You can define the area you want to render based on the frames you set. Make sure to select the video format you want and note that if you want transparency, you cannot save it as a video—only as images. ## Conclusion and Q&A Surprisingly, I still managed to share all this content in the time allotted. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. The recording will be shared, and we appreciate your participation today. Thank you for listening, and I look forward to seeing you in the next session. ```
